newsitem.title: UK: Bond market wrapup - late European trade.
newsitem.headline: Bond market wrapup - late European trade.

text.p: This is how major world bond markets looked at 1630 GMT on Wednesday.
UNITED STATES - U.S. Treasury prices soared by midday on Wednesday after the government said its June Consumer Price Index (CPI) rose only slightly in June.

The government said the CPI rose 0.1 percent, an even smaller than the modest 0.2 percent increase that economists had anticipated. The core CPI, the CPI without its food and energy items, also rose just 0.1 percent.
Futures: T-bonds at 114-20/32, up 22/32
Eurodollars at 94.23, up 0.01
Cash: Long bond yield 6.48 percent.
GERMANY - Bunds, futures remain firm in late dealings but
off session highs. Market lacks fuel to break consolidative tone
amid fears about Buba response to weak mark.
Futures: Bunds on LIFFE at 102.67, up 0.35
Euromarks at 96.79, up 0.02
Cash: 10-year Bund yield 5.57 percent.
BRITAIN - Gilts waded through a data-packed session and
ended up with modest gains, helped out by a surprise fall in UK
wages growth.
The September gilt future settled 10/32 higher at 114-14, off a midsession peak of 114-19, but well into the black nonetheless.
Futures: Long gilts on LIFFE at 114.62, up 0.5
Eurosterling at 92.84, up 0.01
Cash: 10-year gilt yield 7.05 percent.

FRANCE - French September bond futures ended slightly higher on Wednesday in a market which lacked conviction with investors waiting for Monday's publication of an audit into France's public finances, dealers said.
A slightly weaker than expected U.S. June CPI figure allowed the notionnel to test resistance at 130.32 but the contract failed to break through.
Futures: Long bond on MATIF at 130.3, up 0.16
PIBOR at 96.51, up 0.02
Cash: 10-year bond (OAT) yield 5.46 percent.

ITALY - Italy's debt market ended a lacklustre session with Btp futures little changed on previous closing levels. Traders said the market had put the downturn of Monday and Tuesday behind it but had no clear direction and was just holding in line with other European bond markets.

Market attention was still focused on the dollar's strength which was preventing European bonds from moving higher. "Those hoping for statements from the German government which might give the mark a boost have been disappointed," one trader said.
Futures: Long bond on LIFFE at 135.9, up 0.36
Eurolira at 93.34, unchanged
Cash: 10-year bond (BTP) yield 6.56 percent.
JAPAN - The key September 10-year Japanese government bond futures contract ended higher on Wednesday due to short-covering, traders said.

"Those who had earlier sold for hedging purposes ahead of the Bank of Japan governor's news conference bought back after seeing that JGBs had a solid bottom," said a trader for a city bank's securities unit. Futures: JGB future on LIFFE compared with Tokyo close at 124.94, up 0.19
Euroyen at 99.32, unchanged
Cash: 10-year JGB yield 2.53 percent.
EUROBONDS - New issue business on Wednesday was concentrated on the dollar and sterling, the two currencies riding highest on the forex markets.

Bank Nederlandse Gemeenten's bid to penetrate British institutional demand gained plaudits, with dealers saying the 20 basis points reoffer spread on the 300 million stg 10-year offering represented very fair value.
